A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mean Flow Policy Optimization, with matching authors, methods and retained experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite experiments, component ablations, estimator analyses and a two-dimensional toy experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds HumanoidBench and AntMaze experiments, additional baseline comparisons, component timing and likelihood-error diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same MeanFlow policy, average divergence network, adaptive two-proposal velocity estimator, losses and sampling procedure. The newly evaluated BPTT and SAC-GMM methods are comparators, not revisions to MFPO.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained MuJoCo, DeepMind Control Suite and toy coverage, v2 adds three HumanoidBench tasks—Sit Simple, Crawl and Balance Simple—and AntMaze-v1, v3 and v4. These extend evaluation to additional high-dimensional control tasks and multi-goal navigation.

E2.justification: SAC-Flow joins the existing MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite comparisons. New appendix comparisons evaluate SAC-GMM with 4 and 16 components, MEow, and a BPTT-trained MeanFlow policy. FPMD and RFM are discussed but are not reported as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds progressive component timing controls, real-task likelihood evaluation against a 1000-step Euler reference, GMM component-count comparisons, and AntMaze trajectory evaluation after 100k interactions. Table D1 becomes Table 2 and changes DIME's reported target-smoothing coefficient from 0.005 to 1; whether retained experiments were rerun is unspecified.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.2 measures the incremental cost and benefit of MeanFlow, ADN and adaptive velocity estimation. E.3 adds training-time likelihood-error and estimator-variance diagnostics, while E.6 examines multimodal exploration using AntMaze trajectories and entropy-related controls. Existing ablations and hyperparameter analyses are retained under new numbering.

E5.justification: Comparable benchmark curves retain means over five random seeds with standard-deviation shading, and the added benchmark comparisons use the same convention. No increased run count, new confidence-interval procedure or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds HumanoidBench returns, SAC-Flow results, GMM/MEow comparisons, AntMaze trajectories and ADN-error findings. Table 3 reports component results ranging from 2.45 hours and 0.52 normalized return for the diffusion-policy control to 2.81 hours and 1.00 for full MFPO. Table 1 adds SAC-Flow's 0.96 ms inference latency, and Figure 2 lowers the final MaxEntDP Humanoid-v3 points.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.5 adds Propositions B.1 and B.2, proofs for soft policy evaluation and improvement, and an MFPO convergence argument. These rely on accurate likelihood estimation, sufficiently expressive function classes and an infinite-sample limit for velocity estimation. The earlier derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claim: few-step MeanFlow policies enable competitive performance with reduced computational cost through likelihood approximation and adaptive velocity estimation. Adding HumanoidBench to the supporting experiment list does not redefine that claim.

C2.justification: Appendices E.5–E.6 add explanations involving GMM component selection, normalizing-flow architectural constraints, SAC's unimodality and BPTT's entropy-free mode collapse. The new impact statement discusses prospective robotics benefits. The existing limitation that strong performance requires two sampling steps remains.

D1.justification: The advertised code location changes from MFPolicy/MFPO to dongxiaoyi-xyz/MFPO. Appendix D adds SAC-Flow's implementation link, framework and hyperparameters, and explicitly describes batch-size harmonization. These are limited additions to the existing implementation documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and references for FPMD, RFM and SAC-Flow, plus positioning against GMM and normalizing-flow policies through MEow. HumanoidBench and soft-Q-learning references are also added. These extend the literature coverage without replacing the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 expands the appendix organization, adds acknowledgements and an impact statement, edits affiliation/correspondence text, and converts numbered citations to author–year style. The revision does not extensively rewrite the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with substantially different typography, headers and placement of displays. v2 adds four figures and a component-results table, expands comparator legends and table columns, and renumbers appendix displays continuously. Some new captions contain incorrect panel references, notably Figures 8–9.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central claims: Table 3 quantifies component costs, Figure 6 tests likelihood accuracy on a control task beyond v1's toy visualization, and broader baselines plus HumanoidBench and AntMaze probe performance and multimodal exploration. These gains outweigh minor caption errors. The convergence analysis remains conditional, and the maze evidence is qualitative.
